## Findings
- claim-1: In the integral symmetric-function model, \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\); the Schur functions are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis, \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of shapes outside \((n-r)^r\), and \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong H^\ast(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\). [source-2@L1310-L1330|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The paper explicitly extends its type-\(A\) argument from characteristic-zero fields to the integral coinvariant algebra \(H^\ast(G/B,\mathbb Z)\). [source-2@L1339-L1350|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), the source states that \(J_v\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2@L1354-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- claim-4: Theorem 5.4 gives two smaller integral generating sets for \(J_v\) as an ideal of \(H^\ast(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-2@L1380-L1402|claim=formal-document]
- claim-5: The 2024 St. Dizier–Yong paper is identified by DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\); its supplied abstract says it proves the minimality conjecture, but supplies neither theorem text nor coefficient hypotheses concerning an integral Schur-span description of \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
- claim-6: The inspected records do not contain an exact external theorem statement asserting the stronger equality \(J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu\), rather than the source’s integral *ideal-generation* statement. Thus this exact Schur-span identification remains ungrounded by a retrieved citable statement.
## Strategy
Use the existing integral statements in source-2@L1310-L1330 and L1354-L1375. A prospective reduction is: the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of \(s_\mu\) with \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\) is an ideal by the integral Littlewood–Richardson rule, since every nonzero term \(s_\nu\) in \(s_\lambda s_\mu\) has \(\nu\supseteq\mu\); box-external terms vanish in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). Together with source-2’s integral ideal-generation statement, this would yield equality with \(J_v\), but it must be backed by an exact LR citation/locator.

Bound the inspected record set to the supplied source-2 excerpts and DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\) abstract. The critic-mentioned arXiv identifier `0809.2981v2` is an unverified retrieval lead, not inspected evidence.

## Gaps
No external-search or retrieval action was supplied. Hence no queries, database results, arXiv record, full text for DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\), or exact LR-theorem locator was inspected.

The DOI abstract establishes neither the coefficient ring nor a definition or Schur-span description of \(J_v\). The current formal excerpts state integral ideal generation, not the requested equality verbatim. Thus no new citable external statement grounding the equality has been obtained.

## Next
Retrieve and inspect `0809.2981v2` and the full text corresponding to DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\); record title, authors, theorem/definition numbers, and coefficient hypotheses. Obtain an exact citable integral Littlewood–Richardson locator, then present the span equality explicitly as a derived consequence, not a verbatim theorem, unless a later source states it directly.
